skill.name: gpt-series-reasoning-style
skill.description: Apply a disciplined reasoning and delivery process for numeric checks, coding tasks, acceptance review, and multi-agent coordination. It emphasizes evidence, explicit completion levels, and verification before claiming work is finished.
skill.summary: A verification-first workflow for reliable delivery and coordinated AI work.
skill.author: jadeyingwah

security_audit.summary: All 65 static findings are false positives based on their cited snippets. They identify documentation examples, installation paths, Markdown syntax, a standard ignore entry, or entropy heuristics rather than executable malicious behavior; no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was evidenced.

remediation.issue: Installation documentation encourages copying skills into hidden home-directory paths and describes symlink setup.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact files changed and recommend reviewing paths and symlink targets before running setup commands.

remediation.issue: Static analysis reports many heuristic entropy findings on Markdown files.
remediation.suggestion: Keep documentation in plain text and configure scanners to distinguish Markdown prose from encoded payloads.

remediation.issue: The self-check script parses Markdown fence markers.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the parser limited to local file validation and avoid shell execution or user-controlled command construction.

content.value_statement: AI work can appear complete while important checks remain undone. This skill adds a structured planning, execution, review, and evidence process so users can validate results before delivery.
actual_capabilities: Structures tasks into planning, execution, review, and delivery stages.
Defines evidence-based completion levels for finished work.
Supports numeric checks and independent verification of outputs.
Provides role guidance for commander, executor, and reviewer agents.
Offers rules for planning, review, and multi-agent coordination.
limitations: It does not independently guarantee that a result is correct.
It does not replace domain expertise, tests, or security review.
It requires the host agent to read and follow the relevant guidance.
It does not define creative quality standards for every project.

use_cases.title: Review a completed coding task
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to inspect changed files, run relevant checks, and record evidence before reporting completion.

use_cases.title: Coordinate multiple AI agents
use_cases.description: Assign clear roles, boundaries, and handoff evidence so parallel agents produce reviewable work.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads and AI workflow designers

use_cases.title: Validate calculations and reports
use_cases.description: Apply explicit arithmetic checks and independent review steps before accepting a numeric result.

prompt_templates.title: Start a verified task
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this task in clear stages. State the expected deliverable and the evidence required before calling it complete.

prompt_templates.title: Check a delivered change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the completed work against the request. Identify missing checks, run or propose verification steps, and separate verified facts from assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate specialist agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent plan with commander, executor, and reviewer roles. Define inputs, outputs, handoffs, and independent evidence for each stage.

prompt_templates.title: Run an adversarial acceptance review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this delivery as a skeptical reviewer. Look for false completion, untested claims, arithmetic errors, and unverified assumptions. Report findings with concrete evidence and remaining actions.

output_examples.input: A developer says a bug fix is complete but provides no test output.
output_examples.output: The review marks the claim as unverified, requests the relevant test or reproduction evidence, and lists the exact remaining acceptance checks.

output_examples.input: Three agents return overlapping implementation suggestions.
output: A coordinator compares the suggestions against the task requirements.
A reviewer selects a supported approach and records unresolved trade-offs before delivery.

output_examples.input: An analysis contains a total derived from several values.
output_examples.output: The workflow requests an independent recalculation, shows the checked inputs, and labels the result verified only after the values agree.

best_practices: Define completion evidence before starting implementation.
Separate self-reported progress from independently verified results.
Keep handoffs concise, explicit, and tied to the original acceptance criteria.
anti_patterns: Claiming completion without opening or testing the relevant output.
Using multiple agents without clear ownership or review boundaries.
Treating plausible prose or arithmetic as proof without checking it.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps structure verification-first work for coding, calculations, delivery review, and multi-agent coordination.

faq.question: Does it guarantee correctness?
faq.answer: No. It improves the verification process but cannot replace tests, expertise, or independent judgment.

faq.question: Can I use it for small questions?
faq.answer: The guidance is intended for tasks where planning, delivery, or verification has meaningful value.

faq.question: How does it handle multiple agents?
faq.answer: It assigns roles and defines explicit handoffs, outputs, and review evidence for coordinated work.

faq.question: What is false completion?
faq.answer: False completion is reporting success without checking the requested artifact, behavior, or acceptance evidence.

faq.question: Can it review creative quality?
faq.answer: It can verify stated requirements and evidence, but it does not set universal standards for creative quality.
